## Not adopted

### `memory-capture.sh` — deferred

*The-Claude-Protocol · `af754ef` · ruled in round-008-claude-protocol*

Right idea (frictionless capture), poor implementation: the comment body is reconstructed by regex over the shell command string (:28) — quoted ids, heredocs, and -m forms silently capture nothing — and the tag vocabulary is hardcoded Swift/AppKit terms (:57-60) from its origin project. The recall tool advertises an 'investigation' type this hook can never produce. Its provenance idea (source + bead fields, docs/memory-architecture.md:50-54) was adopted now as the optional Source: line in project/learnings.md. Re-open capture automation only if manual learnings capture demonstrably loses entries; any rebuild targets our learnings.md format.

### `teach` — out of scope

*mattpocock_skills · `84fdeff` · ruled in round-001-council-consolidation*

Not a software skill. It builds a multi-session personal learning workspace with missions, HTML lessons, learning records and spaced retrieval; its own examples are yoga and theoretical physics. Out of scope by KIND, not by redundancy — nothing duplicates it. Retained intact and self-contained if a personal-productivity catalog is ever wanted.

### `wait-what` — out of scope

*mattpocock_skills · `84fdeff` · ruled in round-001-council-consolidation*

A 7-line conversational-repair macro: re-pitch the last message in Simplified Technical English. Output is consumed by a person, not the software system. Nearly free to reinstate later — user-invoked, zero always-on context cost.
